question: Which of the following pairs will be in the same homologous series?
solution:
The correct answer is** CH3COCH3 and C2H5COCH3**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• CH3COCH3

 
 
• **​Acetone** is an organic compound that is very flammable. This organic solvent is also known as **propanone **and has the chemical formula C3H6O.
 
• It is present in vehicle, plant, tree, and forest fire exhaust. It is also found in the human body, typically in the form of **blood and urine.**
 
• It has **no color **and is **volatile.** It can be dissolved in water, ether, or ethanol, and it has an unpleasant, floral, or **pungent** scent. As a solvent and antiseptic, it is widely used.
 
• Acetone was first made by **alchemists**. Dry distillation of metal acetates is used to make it. At the moment, **propylene **can either directly or indirectly produce acetone.
 
• The **cumene** process produces nearly** 83% of acetone**. Acetone can also be made in other, more traditional ways.
 
 
 
• C2H5COCH3
 
 
• ​2-Butanone, also known as **METHYL ETHYL KETONE**, is the above-mentioned compound. Its molecular mass, C2H5COCH3, is 72.1057 g/mol.
 
• Methyl ethyl ketone is a colorless, relatively volatile liquid with a pleasant, pungent odor.
 
• **20°F flash point,** heavier than air vapors.
 
• It is stable during normal **transportation** and does not react with water or many common substances.
 
• It affects the throat, eyes, and nose. Toxic substances may result from **combustion**.
 
• Butanone is a naturally occurring product. It is produced by some trees and can be found in trace amounts in some **fruits and vegetables.**
 
• Additionally, **vehicle and truck **exhausts release it into the air.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hom**ologous series

 
 
• **​**A homologous series is a group of compounds that share** similar chemical properties **and functional groups that differ from the next member by **CH₂**.
 
• In organic compounds with the same general formula, **carbon chains** of varying lengths have been observed.
 
• The homologous series members all belong to the **same functional group.**
 
• All members use the same **general formula**.
 
• Because they belong to the same functional group, their chemical properties are nearly** identical.**
 
• There is a common method of **preparation** among members.
